The offset builds a vertex where more than three faces meet (a floor of four facets falling 1 degree to a drain, and its corners where two walls meet two facets) as the two vertices and the new edge the four offset planes give, where upstream fails the shell (1001): `SmOffsetGeometryCreation`'s tangency tolerance is half a degree, not two (the facets, 1.2 degrees apart, are intersected, not left to meet by extending their trims); `TrimExtendedEdge` keeps a trim point within 5 degrees of tangent where the curve crosses the surface (only a touch is dropped); and, where two faces' offsets cut the edge at a vertex all of whose edges are convex (or all concave), the edge ends at the cut it reaches first from its other end, not at the one nearest the vertex.

`CreateFilletBrep` sets each solver's trace reach before the corners (`sm_ExtendTraceToItsRails`): where the base surfaces' domains extended by the solver's factor (half their size) do not reach as far as a rail can lie from the edge (`r / tan(t/2)`, `t` the smallest angle between the faces' planes along it, `r` the largest radius over the trace, a variable round's law included), they reach twice that and `r` more, in the parameter directions that run across the edge (`GetDomainExtension`), so a blend wider than its faces is traced to its rails instead of being clamped at the extended domain's border; and `RailEdgeuseIntersect` runs a straight side edge on a plane on along its line as far, so a rail meeting the side edge's line past the edge's end is found (WR-609, WR-610, #960; the fork's tangency-labs/smlib@a9277fd and @6e77631).

`SmFilletVertex::CalcRailIntEdgeuse` places a rail's end found on a side edge at the rail's base surface evaluated with out-of-bounds evaluation on (the surface continued, as `RailEdgeuseIntersect`'s solve over the extended domain found it), not clamped to the surface's own domain, where a rail meeting a side edge's line just past the edge's end (a cliff overflow, with `fillet_trace_reaches_rails`) was put on the edge's end vertex, off the rail by the square of that distance over twice the radius, and taken as meeting the side edge (WR-630, #960/#1467; the fork's tangency-labs/smlib@3f22e97).

SolidCraft's cliff overflow (WR-631, #960; the fork's tangency-labs/smlib@8ba4667 and later, rev 68fb9162): with `fillet_refuse_rails_leaving_faces` (which must be on too; this flag does nothing without it), a convex blend whose rails leave the faces they roll on across cliffs (an opening's rim, the body's outline) is built on the faces' continuations and the material it removes is subtracted from the body, instead of being refused.

With `fillet_trace_reaches_rails`, `RailEdgeuseIntersect` runs a straight side edge on along its line past its far end only, never behind the corner: past the end at the filleted edge's vertex it lies on the far side of the filleted edge, outside the sector the blend fills, where no rail of it can be, and where (with the faces continued as themselves) a mirror image of the ball can be solved for (WR-643, #960; the SolidCraft fork's tangency-labs/smlib@7224896, branch `replay/1.0.1`).

With `fillet_trace_reaches_rails`, `RailEdgeuseIntersect` evaluates a side edge's linear B-spline UV trim with out-of-bounds evaluation on over the run-on range (on its own copy of the trim), so it continues along its line past its ends as a line trim does.

`SmFilletGeom::TrimRailCurves` trims a rail at its own knot next to the parameter its end vertex drops to, inside the trim, when the rail between the two is no longer than the target B-rep's zone tolerance (`sm_SnapRailEndToKnot`): a trim there left an end span shorter than the tolerance with coincident control points, an internal point singularity of the rail and of the face curves trimmed with it, which the body check refuses.

`SmAdvSurfaceIntersector::FindInteriorCurves` traces a start point whose surface normals are within 5 degrees (guess) or 2 degrees (solution) on probation instead of skipping it, keeping the trace only when it closes into a crossing loop whose box diagonal exceeds twice the tolerance; starts below `2 tol / model size` radians are still skipped and rejected traces (and their start points) are remembered so neighbouring starts are not retraced.
`SmSurfaceIntersector::IsPointOnStartPoint` compares the squared distance of each surface point with the squared tolerance instead of with the tolerance itself (WR-51).
`MakeDupin` uses `1/sqrt(abs(k1))` for the bottom hyperbola's second axis, matching the top conjugate branch at unequal-curvature saddle points (WR-69).

`SmFilletIntersector::ComputeNextPoint`, where the solver's offsets change along the trace (`OffsetRadiiCanChange`, a variable round), solves the fillet at the span's five test shares (a step of that share from its start) and rejects the span where a solution's contact lies farther than the approximation tolerance from its Hermite rail.

`SmBrep::GlueVertices` joins the pair of shells of every region both vertices are in (each other pair's children transferred with its wire edges, the emptied shell removed), not only the last pair its search finds: a solid's vertex is in a shell of the solid's region and one of the infinite region's, so where a face that alone held two parts of a body together was deleted, gluing the parts again at a vertex left the other region's pair apart, and the check reported an edge use and its radial in two shells (WR-607; SolidCraft change, tangency-labs/smlib 661f79c).

`SmPrimitiveCreation::CreateBox` returns the status of each face it makes (a plane that cannot be made, a face whose making fails even after the face was made, such as a box far smaller than the tolerance whose top face closes up on its bottom one) and of its `StitchAndOrient`, and makes no face on a side of zero extent.

`SmBrep::DeleteFilletFace` removes a ring fillet (a round all the way round a boss's foot or rim: two closed tangent rails, one vertex each, and at most one seam) with the fork's `SmRingFilletRemoval`: the sharp edge is the intersection of the two tangent faces' surfaces within their natural domains (an exact circle for a boss), the tangent face's seam runs on to it along its line, and the rails become it; a removal that would need a surface or a curved edge continued past its domain is refused before the B-rep changes.

`SmFeatureExecutive::DoDefeature` refuses a feature whose base patch could not be built (`SmFeature::BuildPatches` leaves `m_bBaseRebuilt` FALSE), with `SM_ERR` (the loop edge of the first unfilled loop in the error), and puts the base B-rep back as it was before the call; the executive is left with no features.

`SmMerge::ManifoldBoolean` refuses a union (`SM_ERR`, the face in the error) when a face its STEP 6 would delete has the infinite region on one side and a solid region on the other: deleting it would merge that solid into the outside.

`SmCurve::SimpleCoincidenceChecker` returns a candidate coincidence range whose curves' separation points to opposite sides at its two ends (both separations longer than `SM_EFF_ZERO` scaled by the ends' size) as the one crossing `LocalCurveIntersect` finds inside it, started where the separation taken as linear between the ends vanishes (`SM_ERR` when none is found).

`SmFace::GetPointsInFace` samples a rectangularly trimmed face from its UV domain's minimum: each column starts at the domain's minimum u plus the column increment and each row at the domain's minimum v plus the row increment, and the column increment is the domain's u length over the number of columns plus one.
`sm_CheckSeamCrossing` returns `false` (no seam crossed) for a surface closed in neither direction (`!closed_u && !closed_v`).
`DoIntersection`'s start-point loop fails with [`crate::SolidError::InvalidInput`] once its traces have taken [`MAX_START_LOOP_TRACE_STEPS`] `ComputeNextPoint` calls together.

`SmEdgeDefinition::Imprint` makes no edge for a definition whose two ends are one proto vertex and land on one vertex in each B-rep (`GetFinalVertex`), when its curve is a speck on that vertex (9 samples, ends included, all within each B-rep's vertex tolerance and within the definition's own tolerance, which its edge would have) and another definition of the same proto edge is imprinted between two distinct vertices in each B-rep.

The ASCII database writer (`SmDatabaseIO`, `SmBrep::WriteToFile(.., SM_ASCII, ..)`) writes each double in the shortest form that reads back as the same double, in exponent notation (`3.0000000000000004e-1`), where upstream's stream is `fixed` with precision 16 (`%.16f`): that keeps 16 digits after the point, fewer than 17 significant digits below 1, so `0.3` plus 1 ULP reads back as `0.3` and a sphere's read-back volume drifts by 1.3e-5 relative (WR-655, the loss seen in #1485).
